newsitem.title: USA: ABN AMRO says files for NYSE listing.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says files for NYSE listing.

text.p: Dutch banking group ABN AMRO Holding NV said Wednesday it had filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said in a statement it had filed a registration statement with the SEC to list its American Depository Shares (ADSs). Each ADS will represent one of its ordinary shares.
Trading on the exchange is expected to start May 21 under the symbol "AAN."

The company also said that in connection with the New York Stock Exchange listing it intended to re-offer to U.S. investors about 14 million ordinary shares, or about one percent of its outstanding ordinary shares.
A registration statement relating to secondary offering has been filed with the SEC but has not become effective.
The syndicate for the secondary offering will be jointly lead managed by ABN AMRO Rothschild, a division of ABN AMRO Chicago Corp, and Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
